trigger: user-supplied replacement OPENCODE GO credential (account 7776004) following the repeated upstream failures in this round
severity: blocking for model-backed lanes; not a product defect

diagnosis.before: the opencodex provider entry carried a stale upstream credential. Called directly against the upstream chat endpoint it returned HTTP 401 Invalid API key. Through the proxy this surfaced intermittently: a 12-call probe returned 6x200 + 6x401, and later windows were 8x401, 8x401, 8x200 - i.e. the proxy served a mix of a live and a dead credential rather than a clean quota refusal.
diagnosis.correction_to_earlier_report: the earlier 'HTTP 429 upstream quota' reading was incomplete. 429 was real in the bridge log (7 occurrences) but the stale-credential 401 is the condition that actually kept the checker lane from finishing; both belong to the same provider-credential defect class.
diagnosis.new_credential_check: GET /v1/models 200; POST /v1/chat/completions 200 with real content from deepseek-v4.1-flash; the upstream requires an x-opencode-session header, which the proxy supplies.

action_taken: backed up the pre-change provider config to .hgk/preflight/R5-compiler/opencodex-config.backup-20261010.json

wrote the replacement credential into the opencodex provider entry via `ocx config set providers.opencode-go.apiKey` (value read from the user's attachment on stdin; never echoed, never logged, not present in any chat or evidence file)

`ocx restart` refused: 'running proxy identity could not be attested'. The running proxy nevertheless picked up the new credential; no forced restart was performed, to avoid disturbing the user's Codex routing (doctor already flags custom-local routing as at risk after restart).
post-change probe through the round's bridge: 30/30 consecutive HTTP 200
side_effects_disclosed: the user's opencodex provider config was modified (one credential field); a backup of the previous file is kept in the round directory
no process was killed, no service restarted, no Codex routing changed
the proxy still runs with the credential it loaded at start plus the refreshed value; the two are indistinguishable to me from the outside
residual_risk: the proxy identity could not be attested, so I cannot prove from the outside which credential a given request used. The 30/30 clean run is behavioural evidence, not an attested statement.
if the proxy cached a credential per worker, a stale worker could still produce a 401 later; the monitor below is the detection mechanism

monitoring.rule: any lane running >10 minutes; escalate when the same abnormal block class repeats more than 4 times
monitoring.action_on_breach: kill the lane, verify whatever it already wrote host-side, record the incident, report

secret_handling: the credential value is never reproduced in this file, in the chat, or in any evidence artefact. Only its length, prefix class and a truncated sha256 were used for verification.
